- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of forecast horizon).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then decline too sharply, missing sustained or delayed price rebounds.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias — overreacts to recent spikes, underestimating persistence or volatility.
- Forecasts often overshoot after sharp price spikes, then fail to adjust downward quickly enough.
- Model underestimates downward price corrections after high volatility periods, especially when true outcomes show sharp drops.
- Forecasts are overly smooth — fail to capture abrupt reversals or sudden drops in price, particularly in the last 5–10 days of the forecast.
- Model tends to ignore or underweight recent low-price periods, leading to persistent overestimation.
- Forecasts show lag in responding to true price drops — often takes 2–3 days for model to adjust downward.
- Model overconfident in upward trends — fails to account for structural or policy-driven price corrections.
- Forecasts are overly optimistic in the short term (1–3 days) but become more accurate later in the horizon (5–10 days), suggesting a lag in calibration.
